newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST--Italy seen issuing 12.5 trln lire BTPs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST--Italy seen issuing 12.5 trln lire BTPs.

text.p: The Italian treasury is expected to issue between 11 and 15 trillion lire of long and medium term paper at its end of the month auction, of which two trillion lire will be 30-year fixed rate bonds (BTPs), analysts said.
They forecast the average amount of paper to be issued at 12.5/13.0 trillion lire for the auction which will take place on January 30 and January 31.
In February, some 11 trillion lire of floating rate certificates (CCTs) will mature as well as 10 trillion lire zero coupon certificates (CTZs), analysts said.

"It's hard to forecast what will happen next month because of January's very positive data on the public sector borrowing requirement," one analyst said. On top of that, "we do not know how the month's requirements will be divided between the two days of auction" (January 30-31).

The Treasury announced on Thursday that it will issue on January 30 a new tranche of February 1 2007 BTP with a reduced coupon of 6.75 percent, a new November 2026 BTP with a 7.25 percent coupon, and a third tranche of January 1 2004 CCT with a first coupon of 3.45 percent.
Settlement date for these bills is February 2.

The Treasury also announced that the January 31 auction will include the fifth tranche of the 6.0 percent coupon BTP February 1 2000 and of the 6.25 percent coupon BTP February 1 2002. Settlement date for these bills is February 4.
